origins.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

gates.says: all 2 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-which-kind: Given this page and this question without its key, which one option does the page support?
recorded.pass:q-which-kind: two independent agents, each given the page and the unkeyed question
recorded.because:q-which-kind: Pitfall 1 says the difference between static and unbound ClassName::method is whether the method is static or an instance method. / The page says both use ClassName::method syntax and the difference is whether the method is static or an instance method.
recorded.prompt:q-private-constructor: Given this page and this question without its key, which one option does the page support?
recorded.pass:q-private-constructor: two independent agents, each given the page and the unkeyed question
recorded.because:q-private-constructor: The page answers: only where that constructor is accessible, the same access rules as new apply. / The page says a private-constructor reference works only where that constructor is accessible, the same access rules as new.

recorded.rule: Q2 v2: a giveaway, read from the question's own text alone
recorded.prompt:q-which-kind: Answer ONLY from this question's own text: its stem and its options. Use no knowledge of the subject at all; treat every term as a word you have never met. Pick an option only when the wording itself singles it out: it is longer or more specific than the others, it repeats words from the stem, the others carry absolute terms such as 'always' or 'never', the stem's grammar fits it alone, or it restates the stem. A cue decides only when it clearly singles out one option over every other; a weak cue, or one another option shares, decides nothing. Otherwise answer 'none'. Say which cue decided it, or that none did.
recorded.pass:q-which-kind: an independent agent given Q2_PROMPT, the stem and the options, never the page
recorded.outcome:q-which-kind: from the question's text alone, the reader picked none; the key is 'a'
recorded.because:q-which-kind: Each option echoes a stem word ('method', 'class name', 'reference'). They are the same length and have the same grammar, so no cue singles one out.
recorded.prompt:q-private-constructor: Answer ONLY from this question's own text: its stem and its options. Use no knowledge of the subject at all; treat every term as a word you have never met. Pick an option only when the wording itself singles it out: it is longer or more specific than the others, it repeats words from the stem, the others carry absolute terms such as 'always' or 'never', the stem's grammar fits it alone, or it restates the stem. A cue decides only when it clearly singles out one option over every other; a weak cue, or one another option shares, decides nothing. Otherwise answer 'none'. Say which cue decided it, or that none did.
recorded.pass:q-private-constructor: an independent agent given Q2_PROMPT, the stem and the options, never the page
recorded.outcome:q-private-constructor: from the question's text alone, the reader picked none; the key is 'c'
recorded.because:q-private-constructor: Only (a) has an absolute term ('Anywhere at all'), which leaves (b) and (c). (c) repeats 'constructor', but (a) and (b) repeat 'reference', so the echo is shared and weak.

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's discriminating readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-which-kind:b: Does a passage of the page rule this wrong option out?
recorded.pass:q-which-kind:b: an independent agent given the page and the keyed question
recorded.outcome:q-which-kind:b: the page rules this option out
recorded.because:q-which-kind:b: Pitfall 1 says of ClassName::method 'The difference is whether the method is static or an instance method', and A2 says the compiler decides based on the method declaration, not how the class name is written.
recorded.prompt:q-which-kind:c: Does a passage of the page rule this wrong option out?
recorded.pass:q-which-kind:c: an independent agent given the page and the keyed question
recorded.outcome:q-which-kind:c: the page rules this option out
recorded.because:q-which-kind:c: Pitfall 1 ('The difference is whether the method is static or an instance method') and A4 (the compiler checks whether 'method' is static or an instance method of ClassName) name the method's declaration, not the context the reference is written in.
recorded.prompt:q-private-constructor:a: Does a passage of the page rule this wrong option out?
recorded.pass:q-private-constructor:a: an independent agent given the page and the keyed question
recorded.outcome:q-private-constructor:a: the page rules this option out
recorded.because:q-private-constructor:a: The interview insight answers '(Only where that constructor is accessible, e.g. inside the class itself — the same access rules as new apply)', so a reference does not skip the access check.
recorded.prompt:q-private-constructor:b: Does a passage of the page rule this wrong option out?
recorded.pass:q-private-constructor:b: an independent agent given the page and the keyed question
recorded.outcome:q-private-constructor:b: the page rules this option out
recorded.because:q-private-constructor:b: The same passage says only where the constructor is accessible, with the same access rules as new, so a reference does not widen private access to subclasses.
